learn: The seven elements of art are line, shape, form, value, colour, texture and space.
Artists combine elements to create meaning and mood.
Learning the elements gives you a vocabulary to make and discuss art.
check: Which is an element of art?
How many elements of art are there?
Elements give you a vocabulary to...
lessons.try: Create a seven-box chart with a small drawing showing each element.

learn: Line quality is the character of a line: thick, thin, heavy, light, smooth or rough.
Expressive lines show emotion: jagged lines feel tense; flowing lines feel graceful.
Contour lines describe edges; gesture lines capture movement quickly.
lessons.try: Do three 30-second gesture drawings of a family member moving.

learn: Artists turn shapes into forms by adding value and overlapping.
Geometric forms appear in architecture; organic forms in nature and sculpture.
Drawing basic forms (cube, cylinder, sphere, cone) is the foundation of drawing objects.
check: Shapes become forms when you add...
lessons.try: Draw a cube, cylinder, sphere and cone with shading.

learn: Every colour has three properties: hue (its name), value (lightness) and intensity (brightness or dullness).
Adding a colour's complement lowers its intensity, making it duller.
High-intensity colours grab attention; low-intensity colours recede.
check: Adding a complement makes a colour...
lessons.try: Mix red with tiny amounts of green to make a scale from bright to dull red.

learn: Triadic colours are three hues evenly spaced on the wheel, like red, yellow and blue.
Split-complementary uses one hue and the two next to its complement.
Harmonies help colours look good together.
check: Red, yellow and blue form a...
lessons.try: Paint a design using a triadic colour scheme.

learn: Colours carry meanings that can differ across cultures.
In many Western cultures, white is linked to weddings; in some East Asian traditions, white is linked to mourning.
Artists choose colours with their audience and message in mind.
check: Do colour meanings differ across cultures?
lessons.try: Research what one colour means in two different cultures.

learn: Light comes from a source and creates a pattern on forms: highlight, light, core shadow, reflected light and cast shadow.
The core shadow is the darkest part on the form itself.
Reflected light is a faint lightening on the shadow side from light bouncing off nearby surfaces.
check: The darkest part on the form is the...
How many parts of light logic did we name?
lessons.try: Shade a sphere showing all five parts of light logic.

learn: Pencils range from hard (H) to soft (B). Soft pencils like 4B make darker marks.
Blending stumps smooth graphite. Erasers can lift highlights.
Build value gradually with light layers.
check: An eraser can be used to...
lessons.try: Make value scales with an HB pencil and a 4B pencil. Compare.

learn: Set up a still life with one strong light source.
Squint to see the big shapes of light and dark.
Draw light lines first, then build darks and save highlights.
check: Big shapes of light and dark
Use how many light sources for clear shadows?
What should you save for last?
lessons.try: Draw a still life of three objects with full value.

learn: Two-point perspective uses two vanishing points on the horizon line.
It shows objects, like buildings, seen from a corner.
Vertical lines stay vertical; horizontal edges go to one of the two vanishing points.
check: It shows objects seen from a...
lessons.try: Draw a box in two-point perspective.

learn: The horizon line is at the viewer's eye level.
Objects above the horizon show their bottoms; objects below show their tops.
A low horizon makes things look tall and grand.
check: The horizon line is at the viewer's...
Objects below the horizon show their...
A low horizon makes things look...
lessons.try: Draw a city street with a low horizon, then a high horizon.

learn: Foreshortening makes objects pointing toward you look shorter and wider.
An arm reaching toward the viewer looks short with a big hand.
It creates a dramatic sense of depth.
check: Foreshortening makes objects pointing at you look...
An arm reaching toward you shows a...
lessons.try: Draw your hand reaching toward you, using a mirror.

learn: The head is about five eyes wide.
Ears line up between the eyebrows and the bottom of the nose.
The corners of the mouth line up below the pupils.
check: The head is about how many eyes wide?
Ears line up between the eyebrows and the...
Corners of the mouth line up below the...
lessons.try: Draw a front-view portrait using these proportions.

learn: An adult figure is about seven and a half heads tall.
Elbows line up with the waist; fingertips reach mid-thigh.
Children's heads are larger compared to their bodies.
check: An adult is about how many heads tall?
lessons.try: Draw a stick figure using head units to measure.

learn: Portraits can show a person's job, interests and personality through clothes, setting and objects.
Rembrandt painted many self-portraits over his life, showing himself ageing.
Lighting and pose change how we feel about the person.
check: Who painted many self-portraits over his life?
Objects in a portrait can show...
How we feel about the person
lessons.try: Create a portrait of someone with three objects that tell about them.

learn: A landscape shows natural scenery like mountains, fields and rivers.
The rule of thirds places important elements along lines dividing the image into thirds.
A clear foreground, middle ground and background creates depth.
check: The rule of thirds divides the image into...
What creates depth in a landscape?
lessons.try: Sketch a landscape using the rule of thirds.

learn: Skies are lighter near the horizon and darker higher up.
Water reflects the colours of the sky and objects around it.
Use horizontal strokes for calm water and broken strokes for ripples.
check: Skies are usually lighter near the...
The sky and objects around it
lessons.try: Paint a sunset over a lake with reflections.

learn: Thomas Cole founded the Hudson River School in the 1800s, painting grand American landscapes.
Claude Monet painted the same haystacks and water lilies at different times of day.
Chinese landscape painters showed misty mountains with ink washes.
check: Who founded the Hudson River School?
Monet painted the same scene at different...
lessons.try: Paint the same view at morning and evening like Monet.

learn: Relief printing prints raised surfaces (woodcut, linocut).
Intaglio prints ink from grooves cut into metal (etching, engraving).
Screen printing pushes ink through a mesh stencil, often used on T-shirts.
lessons.try: Look at a T-shirt print and a stamp. Which type is each?

learn: A stencil is a sheet with shapes cut out. Ink or paint passes through the openings.
Positive and negative stencils give opposite results.
Stencils can be layered for multiple colours.
check: A stencil is a sheet with...
lessons.try: Cut a paper stencil and print it twice with different colours.

learn: Prints can be made in large numbers, so they've been used for posters, books and news.
Woodblock prints spread art in Japan during the Edo period.
Many artists use prints to share messages.
check: Why were prints used for posters?
They can be made in large numbers
Woodblock prints were popular in Edo-period...
lessons.try: Design a poster for a cause you care about.

learn: Sculpture uses form, space, texture and mass.
Mass is how heavy or solid a sculpture appears.
Negative space (holes and openings) is part of the design.
check: Mass is how ___ a sculpture appears.
lessons.try: Make a wire or pipe-cleaner sculpture that uses negative space.

learn: Pinch, coil and slab are the three basic hand-building methods.
Score and slip to join pieces.
Keep walls an even thickness so the piece dries and fires evenly.
check: Three hand-building methods are pinch, coil and...
So it dries and fires evenly
lessons.try: Build a slab box with a lid.

learn: Michelangelo carved the marble statue "David" between 1501 and 1504.
Auguste Rodin made "The Thinker" in bronze.
Louise Nevelson made large wooden assemblages painted all one colour.
lessons.try: Create an assemblage from small boxes painted one colour.

learn: African art includes masks, textiles, sculpture and beadwork with deep cultural meaning.
Masks are often used in ceremonies and dances.
Kente cloth from Ghana and mud cloth from Mali carry patterns with meanings.
lessons.try: Design a textile pattern inspired by symbols you create.

learn: Chinese calligraphy is an art of beautiful writing with brush and ink.
Japanese ukiyo-e prints showed everyday life and landscapes.
Indian Mughal paintings were small, detailed and colourful.
lessons.try: Practise brush strokes with watercolour or ink.

learn: The Maya and Aztec created stone sculpture, murals and codices (books).
Mexican muralists like Diego Rivera painted huge public murals in the 1920s and 1930s.
Native American art includes pottery, weaving and beadwork.
check: Mural means a painting on a...
lessons.try: Design a mural about your community.

units.t: Looking at and Talking About Art

learn: Art criticism has four steps: describe, analyse, interpret and judge.
Describe what you see without opinions. Analyse how the elements and principles work.
Interpret the meaning and judge its success with reasons.
lessons.try: Write a four-step critique of a painting by Mary Cassatt.

learn: An artist statement explains your artwork: what you made, how and why.
It helps viewers understand your ideas.
Keep it clear and personal.
check: What, how and why you made art
lessons.try: Write an artist statement for your favourite artwork this year.

learn: Museums collect, preserve and display art.
Curators choose and arrange artworks for exhibitions.
Many museums offer free online collections to explore.
check: Can you explore some museums online?
lessons.try: Take a virtual tour of an art museum and choose a favourite work.
